articles.title: Guardians X-factor that means everything for do-or-die Game 5 vs. White Sox
articles.summary: The playoffs is not the time for making conservative plays; at least that’s what the Cleveland Guardians must have been thinking. After all, they headed to t...
articles.body:
The playoffs is not the time for making conservative plays; at least that's what the Cleveland Guardians must have been thinking. After all, they headed to the road in the ALDS against the Chicago White Sox down 2-0 and had to win at all costs to keep their season alive — even at the cost of their pitching staff's freshness .

In Game 4, the Guardians had to send out Gavin Williams , their starter for Game 5 and one of their best pitchers, to close things out — having him throw 18 pitches to send the series to a do-or-die contest with a 9-5 victory. Before Williams, it looks as though the heavy workload was getting to their best reliever in Cade Smith, who's pitched in all four games of the ALDS thus far. Smith allowed a home run and a walk during his last time out on the mound, which necessitated Williams' relief appearance.

As pointed out by Jon Morosi of MLB Network, the pitch count for the Guardians' hurlers are undoubtedly going to play a part in Game 5 — being a major X-factor that could prove to be the difference between a trip to St. Petersburg for Game 1 of the ALCS against the Tampa Bay Rays and an early exit from the postseason.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Smith has thrown 67 pitches in this series, including 31 in Game 4. Will he be fresh enough to come in relief yet again in Game 5? Foster Griffin, who will be available off the pen in Game 5, threw 53 pitches back on Wednesday in Game 3.

Will Parker Messick, the Guardians' starter who struggled in Game 4, be available just in case the team needs him to? Or has Cleveland burnt their pitchers out enough just to survive?

Only time will tell whether or not Stephen Vogt made the right decisions. But one thing's for sure: he prioritized the Guardians' survival, and they're still alive and kicking, which means that their gambit, up until this point, has worked.

articles.title: Ranking Yankees OF Trent Grisham's Top 10 Landing Spots Ahead of MLB Free Agency
articles.summary: After slugging 34 home runs during the 2025 season, Trent Grisham returned to the New York Yankees when he accepted a one-year, $22.025 million qualifying offer last winter.
articles.body:
After slugging 34 home runs during the 2025 season, Trent Grisham returned to the New York Yankees when he accepted a one-year, $22.025 million qualifying offer last winter.

The 29-year-old failed to match his career year, hitting .211/.308/.395 for a 95 OPS+ with 18 home runs, 59 RBI and 0.6 WAR in 121 games, but he should still draw plenty of interest in free agency.

His age, on-base ability and power in a market that is thin on center field options could still land him a multi-year deal, and his defensive profile means there won't be clear overlap with the market for corner bats like Randy Arozarena and Seiya Suzuki.

A reunion with the Yankees this time around is unlikely, with Spencer Jones emerging alongside Cody Bellinger and Aaron Judge to form next year's outfield, so what jersey will Grisham be wearing in 2027?

Ahead is a rundown of his top 10 speculative suitors.

With Mike Trout, Josh Lowe, Jose Siri and rookie standout Wade Meckler, the Angels have enough in-house talent to stand pat in the outfield. At the same time, Grisham feels like the sort of mid-tier veteran they have targeted in years past, and signing him would allow Trout to return to a corner spot.

The Padres had a revolving door in left field for much of the season before a platoon of Dustin Harris (100 PA, 120 OPS+, 0.9 WAR) and Samad Taylor (175 PA, 124 OPS+, 0.8 WAR) proved to be surprisingly productive. They could run it back with that tandem, but Grisham would provide a more established alternative, and San Diego is plenty familiar with his game.

How many more chances will Evan Carter get to be an everyday center fielder? The 24-year-old was a 1.9-WAR player in 2026, but it was almost solely on the strength of his defense, as he hit .194/.288/.315 for a 76 OPS+ over 455 plate appearances. At this point, he looks more like a glove-only fourth outfielder than the impactful all-around talent he hinted at early in his career.

Disappointing seasons from Dylan Beavers (104 G, 93 OPS+, -0.5 WAR) and Tyler O'Neill (85 G, 92 OPS+, 0.5 WAR) give the Orioles plenty of room to potentially upgrade alongside Colton Cowser in the outfield. The question is how far down the shopping list that will be when pitching is the clear No. 1 priority.

The Blue Jays have already been linked to Seiya Suzuki, and Randy Arozarena fits into a similar bucket as a right-handed hitting, middle-of-the-order corner outfielder. Grisham is unquestionably a tier below those two in terms of expected impact, but he could be a viable fallback plan if they whiff on those top targets.

Projected OF: LF Casey Schmitt, CF Drew Gilbert, RF Jung Hoo Lee

The unmitigated disaster that was the Harrison Bader signing could scare the Giants away from another high-profile addition to the outfield, but it's a group that is far from settled.

Drew Gilbert posted an .812 OPS in 142 plate appearances over the final two months of the season, and he is a plus defender in center field (3 DRS, 5 OAA), so he is a viable in-house candidate if they decide to focus on pitching.

Otherwise, Grisham has the speed and defensive reputation to be a good fit in spacious Oracle Park, and Gilbert could still factor into the starting mix with Casey Schmitt best used as a first baseman or designated hitter.

Each Team's Biggest Roster Hole to Fix in Offseason ⚾

The 10 Greatest MLB Divisional Series Upsets 😮

Projected OF: LF Isaac Collins, CF Kyle Isbel, RF Jac Caglianone

The emergence of Jac Caglianone gives the Royals one clear answer in the outfield after they entered the 2026 season with three genuine question marks, but they could still use an upgrade at the other two spots.

The Royals ranked 28th in OPS for left fielders (.660) and 24th in OPS for center fielders (.658), and the returning trio of Kyle Isbel, Isaac Collins and John Rave probably all profile best as fourth outfielders on a contending team.

Grisham's asking price will be the determining factor in whether the Royals are viable contenders for his services, but he looks like a solid buy-low target to potentially upgrade one of their biggest roster holes.

Projected OF: LF Michael Arroyo, CF Julio Rodríguez, RF Dominic Canzone

Ideally, the Mariners would find a way to retain Randy Arozarena, who was easily their most productive hitter in 2026, though that will likely require a nine-figure commitment as he is arguably the top bat on the market.

They could also opt to go young, using Michael Arroyo in left field after he went 13-for-35 with two doubles and one home run in 15 games as a September call-up, and he has a long track record of production in the minors.

However, Grisham would give them an established everyday option, a viable platoon partner for the right-handed hitting Arroyo and a capable backup for Julio Rodríguez in center field. That last part is important, assuming they decline a $9 million club option on Victor Robles as expected.

Projected OF: LF JJ Bleday, CF Dane Myers, RF Héctor Rodríguez

Aside from a strong season from scrapheap pickup JJ Bleday (105 OPS+, 24 HR, 1.2 WAR), the Reds outfield was sorely lacking in impact production in 2026, and that has been a recurring theme in recent years.

Dane Myers had a 101 OPS+ over 334 plate appearances, but with 19 extra-base hits, a .377 slugging percentage and an OPS that was 99 points higher against left-handed pitching, he is a straight platoon option.

That actually makes the Grisham fit even stronger, as he could pair with Myers in center field and give the team a potential insurance policy while young guys like Héctor Rodríguez and Carlos Jorge work to establish themselves as big league options.

Projected OF: LF Taylor Trammell, CF Lucas Spence, RF Cam Smith

Cam Smith started 139 games in right field for the Astros last season, but left field and center field were as "by-committee" as any team in baseball while they searched for answers.

They ultimately used 12 different starting left fielders and eight different starting center fielders, with no one reaching 40 starts at either position.

Lucas Spence showed enough down the stretch to get a long look this spring, but they can't enter another season hoping the likes of Taylor Trammell, Jake Meyers, Joey Loperfido and Brice Matthews can absorb everyday playing time.

Expect them to cast a wide net in their search for outfield help, and their center field need specifically helps put Grisham high on their list of potential targets.

articles.title: World Series champion says potential MLB lockout could 'absolutely' cause cancelled games next season
articles.summary: World Series champion Nick Swisher said games could "absolutely" be missed next season as MLB and the players association remain far apart on the thought of a salary cap.
articles.body: In a normal year, most MLB teams would already be looking toward next year at this point in the season, as only a few teams remain alive. But what does next season even look like? Major League Baseball and the MLB Players Association are all but guaranteed to have a lockout beginning Dec. 1 , as both sides have diametrically opposed positions on a salary cap. The owners are pushing hard to implement a salary cap, while the players are vehemently opposed. World Series champion Nick Swisher said that games could "absolutely" be missed next season due to a stalemate between the two sides. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "Absolutely, because just like yourself as me, is all of a sudden, you hear the players association speaking this language and the commissioner's office is speaking this language. I immediately knew out of the gate. Plus, just knowing a little bit more under the hood about the last couple of collective bargaining agreements, right?" Swisher told OutKick in a recent interview. The former New York Yankees star noted that Tony Clark is no longer the head of the MLBPA after resigning in February and that Bruce Meyer, who took over for Clark, will want everyone to know how he does business. Swisher said he hopes both sides go to the negotiating table in good faith. "When you get people going to the negotiation table, you're hoping that everyone's trying to go to negotiate a fair deal. You're hoping that both sides aren't trying to go to the negotiation table to win. Because if that's the case, we're in a lot of trouble. Because we're really, really far apart from each other right now, and the last thing we wanna do is slow this train down," Swisher said. Swisher said baseball is "absolutely crushing" right now, with revenue and attendance both up, going so far as to say that the game has never been in a better place. Yet, having spent 12 seasons in the big leagues, he understands just how tough the union is. "Pretty much all other sports are very salary cap-based, and that's kind of been the one thing for the players association and the players union. It's one of the strongest unions in the world for a reason, because they stand up for each other. And I was part of that before. I know the bond, I know the brothership, and, listen, it's a tough union," Swisher said. WILL MAJOR LEAGUE BASEBALL STILL LOCK PLAYERS OUT AFTER 2026 POSTSEASON PROVES OWNERS WRONG? Swisher, like the rest of the baseball world, hopes the two sides can reach an agreement before any games are lost . "I think at the end of the day, man, I'm praying that everything gets itself back on track come the end of the season because I wouldn't wanna slow this train down, man. It's moving too fast right now and we got too many things going on well in our game to be slowing it down right now," Swisher said. BASEBALL OR BABY? During the Division Series, two prominent players were forced to make an impossible decision: Miss their child's birth or leave their team during the postseason to attend the milestone event? About an hour before the San Diego Padres faced the Milwaukee Brewers with their season on the line, All-Star closer Mason Miller went on the paternity list to attend the birth of his child. The Padres won Game 3 and staved off elimination in his absence. New York Yankees starting pitcher Max Fried, on the other hand, said that despite his girlfriend being ready to give birth at any moment, he would pitch in Game 3 no matter what. The Yankees lost the game, so Fried is now free to support his girlfriend for the foreseeable future. Swisher, a father of two children , said he was fortunate to avoid the dilemma Miller and Fried faced . "I was very blessed that I had one child that was born at the beginning of the season and one child that was born in the middle of the season. So, I didn't get presented with this situation where both of these individuals are put in," Swisher said. LEGENDARY SPORTS AGENT WARNS MLB LOCKOUT WOULD BE 'REMARKABLY SELF-DESTRUCTIVE' WITH CBA SET TO EXPIRE "It's hard for me to say that as a father now of two beautiful young girls that I wouldn't want to be there for the birth of my daughter. But once again, I was never put in that position." Having played in numerous postseason games, the former All-Star outfielder said it would have been difficult to miss those opportunities . "At the end of the day, I will tell you this, it's not as often as you think that you get to compete for championships. And for myself, I played in a bunch of playoff games, and we had one great championship run. And it would be really hard for me also to say that I missed out on any of that as well," Swisher said. While it would be difficult to miss a postseason game, the 45-year-old said he couldn't reconcile missing the birth of one of his children. "For myself, at the end of the day, I've never been presented with something like that, so, I really wouldn't even know how to answer that because if I missed the birth of my daughters, either one of them. I feel like that would always bother me," Swisher said. "That would, I would just like – I wasn't there for you. And as a father, that's the one thing that you wanna do is you always wanna be there for your children. So, I can't blame Mason, I can't blame Max." OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD RECOGNIZING THE UNSUNG HEROES While fans see the players on the field and managers making lineup and bullpen decisions, much more goes into running a team behind the scenes . Swisher praised Yankees equipment manager Rob Cucuzza and the entire clubhouse staff for their work. "At the end of the day, I think the unsung heroes are the clubhouse guys, right? The clubhouse, you know, people that, that clean our underwear, right? That wash our jerseys, right, that are up at 4 o'clock in the morning, just unpacking our bags, getting ourselves ready for the next day's worth of work," Swisher, who spoke on behalf of PAYDAY to highlight the low-key legends who helped shape his career, said. "If you don't have those people, if you don't have the engine of your organization, you're not gonna be any good. And the fact that we are so blessed to have someone in New York who does that, who does just that, has an amazing job."

articles.title: Mets Morning News: Game 5, do-or-die
articles.summary: Your Saturday morning dose of Mets and Major League Baseball news, notes, and links.
articles.body:
Teruaki Sato, NPB's first Triple Crown winner since Munetaka Murakami, could make the jump to MLB next season, and he's been linked to the Mets.

Todd Zolecki listed five pressing questions facing the Phillies ahead of this offseason.

The Braves have made a few tweaks to their 40 man roster, adding a lefty pitcher and designating an infielder.

Jackson Chourio's postseason statistics put him in some rarefied air at only 22 years old.

Gavin Williams will start the decisive ALDS Game 5 start for the Guardians, just two days after closing out Game 4.

Colton Cowser believes he can return to form for the Orioles in 2027.

Matthew Roberson of Fangraphs listed the 10 best division series of all time.

The Dodgers have chosen Tarik Skubal and Yoshinobu Yamamoto to start the first two games against the Brewers in the NLCS.

Sean Burke will get the ball first for the White Sox in Game 5 against the Guardians, with the rest of the pitching plan less defined.

The latest MLB proposal for the new CBA is slightly shortening the season, and could be prioritizing quality over quantity with it.

The Brewers went out with a whimper against the Dodgers in last year's NLCS, but this year it could be very different .

Steve Sypa reviewed the 2026 Syracuse Mets season.

65 years ago, the Mets picked the foundational pieces of their first team in the expansion draft.
